title: Holdout manifest, nDCG aggregation and slice protocol
content:
Purpose:
This doc defines the holdout manifest, annotation protocol for pairwise judgments, nDCG aggregation choices, per-slice analysis rules, and regression gating thresholds we will use for onboarding rerank models into production. It is intended to be prescriptive for applied-ml evaluators and partner annotators so that results are comparable across model rollouts.

High-level goals:
- Create a single canonical holdout manifest (stable set of queries + candidate lists) for model comparisons.
- Standardize pairwise labeling instructions and tie treatment.
- Fix nDCG calculation details (log base, position truncation, smoothing) so deltas are reproducible.
- Define slice definitions, minimum sample sizes, and per-slice pass/fail rules for rollouts.
- Provide QC and adjudication steps (IA agreement thresholds, adjudicator flow).

Manifest and sampling scheme:
- Holdout size: target 25k query contexts for full manifest. Split into: 20k main holdout, 3k dev holdout (fast iteration), 2k edge-slice oversamples.
- Candidate pool per query: up to 10 candidates; if more exist choose top-10 baseline-ranked then randomize presentation order for pairwise tasks.
- CSV manifest columns: query_id, query_text, segment, candidate_ids (pipe-delimited), baseline_ranks (pipe-delimited), slice_tags (comma-separated), reason_notes.
- Stable keys: query_id must be UUID4. Do not change candidate_ids across reruns for the same manifest version.

Annotation protocol (pairwise preference):
- Task: present annotator with Query + two candidate responses (A and B). Ask: "Which response would you prefer to show to the user?" Options: A, B, Tie/No preference.
- Tie rules: if annotator selects Tie, count as 0.5 wins to both in basic pairwise summary; for nDCG conversions ties translate to averaged relevance (see below).
- Instruction bullets for annotators: relevance, informativeness, correctness, brevity trade-offs. Include short examples in task UI.
- Minimum judgments per pair: 3 independent annotators. If disagreement (no majority) send to adjudication (senior annotator).
- Annotator metadata: record annotator_id, task_latency_ms, UI_version.

Converting pairwise labels to graded relevance for nDCG:
- For each candidate within a query, we compute an empirical relevance score r_i in [0,1] as: r_i = (wins + 0.5 * ties) / total_pairwise_comparisons_involving_candidate.
- Then convert to graded integer relevance levels 0..3 by thresholds: 0: r < 0.15; 1: 0.15 <= r < 0.40; 2: 0.40 <= r < 0.75; 3: r >= 0.75. These thresholds are tuned to align with historical explicit-graded datasets.
- Keep a copy of raw r_i and also store the derived integer relevance (relevance_level) to ensure auditability.

nDCG calculation details (explicit):
- DCG@k = sum_{i=1..k} (2^{rel_i} - 1) / log2(i + 1). Use log base 2 with i starting at 1 (first position uses denominator log2(2)=1).
- nDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k where IDCG is computed using the sorted relevance_levels descending.
- Report nDCG@1, @3, @5, and @10. Primary metric for gating: nDCG@5.
- Truncation: if fewer than k candidates, compute DCG up to available candidates and divide by IDCG of same length.
- Variance estimation: bootstrap per-query resampling with 10k iterations to get 95% confidence intervals for mean nDCG. Report median and 95% CI.

Aggregation choices and baselines:
- Aggregation is over queries (macro-average) unless explicitly noted. We will publish both macro-average and token-weighted micro-average for transparency.
- Primary baseline: current production reranker v1.8. Baseline snapshot must be included in the manifest metadata (git ref / model id).
- Delta reporting: new_model_nDCG - baseline_nDCG per metric. Report raw delta and p-value from bootstrap-based difference test (two-sided).

Slices and tagging:
- Core slices to always compute: cold-start queries, long-query (>30 tokens), short-query (<6 tokens), intent-specific (support, navigational, transactional), named-entity-heavy (>2 entities), high-ambiguity (multiple plausible answers), and privacy-sensitive (contain PII).
- Slice definition syntax: store slices as boolean expressions over manifest columns (e.g., "long_query := token_count > 30"). Keep slice spec in the manifest repo as plain-text.
- Minimum reliable sample per slice: 300 queries. If a slice falls below 300, include a note and avoid hard gating unless the slice is safety-critical.
- Per-slice gating: no slice should see an nDCG@5 regression beyond -0.8% absolute (i.e., delta < -0.008) unless compensated by large overall gains and approved by ML PM + Safety.

Quality control and adjudication:
- Inter-annotator agreement: compute Krippendorff's alpha on pairwise labels per batch. Flag batch if alpha < 0.55 for review.
- Spam detection: flag annotators with mean task latency < 1/3 of median and agreement < 0.6. Remove their contributions and re-run sampling.
- Adjudication flow: sample 5% of pairs that had non-majority labels for senior review. Maintain an adjudication log with justifications.

Regression gating and rollout checklist:
- Automated checks (must pass): build artifact exists, manifest and baseline ids available, annotation coverage >= 95% pairs judged 3x, bootstrap CI computed, macro-nDCG@5 overall delta >= 0.005 (primary threshold for promotion to canary).
- Manual review checks: per-slice deltas reviewed, safety/relevancy flags resolved, annotator QA passed, documentation updated.
- Canary rollout: start with 1% traffic for 48 hours, monitor live click-through and truncate if observed online metrics degrade beyond thresholds.

Experiment examples and edge-cases:
- Handling ties heavily: if ties > 25% in a query group, treat that query as ambiguous and exclude from primary gating; include separate ambiguity score for analysis.
- Candidate duplication: dedupe identical candidate text before scoring; if duplicates exist keep earliest baseline rank and mark reduced diversity.

Implementation notes (ops):
- Manifest versioning: semantic filenames: holdout-v{major}.{minor}.csv and a meta JSON (manifest meta) recording creation git ref, random seed, exact sampling script used.
- Repro pipeline: store random seed used for randomized steps; every rerun that changes seed creates new manifest version.
- Storage: store raw pairwise judgments in parquet with columns matching CSV manifest plus annotator_id, label, latency_ms, adjudicated_by.

Open questions / items for follow-up:
- Validate integer relevance thresholds against small human-graded explicit dataset V2 (action: Maya to run calibration experiment, due 2026-03-12).
- Decide whether to include micro-average nDCG in gating or only for observability (proposal: observability only).
- Finalize tie-to-relevance mapping cadence for models with many paraphrases.

Checklist before merging manifest to repo:
- [ ] Manifest CSV present and schema validated by manifest-lint script
- [ ] Baseline model id referenced and snapshot recorded
- [ ] Sampling seed recorded and reproducible script attached
- [ ] Annotator instructions reviewed and example bundles included
- [ ] Slice spec file added to repo and minimum sizes verified

Appendix: quick formulas and example
- Example DCG calculation (k=3): rel levels [3,2,1] -> DCG = (2^3-1)/log2(1+1) + (2^2-1)/log2(2+1) + (2^1-1)/log2(3+1) = 7/1 + 3/1.585 + 1/2 = 7 + 1.892 + 0.5 = 9.392
- IDCG for sorted [3,2,1] is same so nDCG@3 = 1.0.

Revision history:

- 2026-03-05 cleaned up manifest schema and checklist (Samir)

Notes: this doc is intended to be pragmatic — keep changes minimal when re-running historical comparisons so results are comparable. For major metric changes publish an explicit migration note.
